direction.premise: A playable illuminated folio: draw on a manuscript and listen to six live parts, with a finished arrangement rather than a loop toy.
direction.composition: Landscape workspace with an open parchment score at center, narrow vertical track ribbon left and instrument inspector right; mobile stacks score and editorial controls beneath a persistent transport.
direction.shapeLanguage: Thin ink rules, square manuscript page corners, notched tab edges, wax-tone corner ornaments; restrained oval seals only for active actions.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Aged vellum and pressed pine with deep malachite ink and muted terracotta notes. No generic dark dashboard cards.
direction.typography: Editorial Georgia display lettering and precise system UI labels in compact sizes.
direction.signature: The staff grid itself is the instrument: touch a pitch to write it, then watch a moving ink playhead sound out the composition.
direction.distinction: Unlike prior arcade and strategy projects, no fullscreen arena or bottom HUD; this is a tactile page-oriented composition desk.

architecture.primaryVerb: Write and replace pitches directly on a living music page.
architecture.physicalFeedback: Immediate pigment fill for a note, moving vertical playhead, playback highlight and optional audible preview.
architecture.spatialRationale: The score is physically presented as a wide manuscript spread; multiple independent instrument tools are arranged at the outer edges while the melody is entered directly on the page. Numbered tabs switch movements without changing the working surface.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Sin Guion focuses on one language practice stage and recording controls; Folkarium keeps a scrollable modal note score as the constant central object, with instrument selectors and audio configuration at its edges.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Instead of choosing answers and recording a spoken response, musicians write pitches on a step grid and audition independently authored musical voices.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Rivals DNA is a narrow single-screen tactical questionnaire; Folkarium uses a wide manuscript composition desk with three working columns and an editable note field.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Notes change the synthesized score and exported musical file, rather than advancing character-choice questions and rating calculations.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Trace Mosaic uses a puzzle square and participant tile tray; Folkarium is a landscape-leaning parchment musical notation spread.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Changing pitch cells changes audio and MIDI events rather than positioning picture fragments on a board.

production.renderer: Native DOM score grid, CSS vellum and Web Audio API. Bespoke local vector fiddle/folio icon.
production.focalAsset: Lined parchment score itself; instrument rails drawn with typography and vector geometry.

motion.character: Ink strokes settle quickly; playback traverses note cells in real time.
motion.action: Tap or drag modal pitches; play, stop, and change instruments.
motion.anticipation: Hover or finger focus highlights the note cell.
motion.response: Note ink appears immediately and preview sounds when audio is unlocked.
motion.followThrough: Playhead passes the edited phrase; changed song auto-saves.
motion.interruption: Cancelling drag stops painting; page visibility suspends playback.
motion.reducedMotion: No animations except essential playhead position in reduced motion.

evidence.expectedChange: Music starts after the explicit play gesture; transport becomes Stop and the playhead moves.
